description:
Donations are tax deductible and we need your support to continue our work. Text-to-donate, text VSRF to 53-555.Show more We’re thrilled to welcome Dr. Elizabeth Mumper, MD, FAAP, to VSRF Live this Thursday.
Dr. Mumper was prominently featured in “An Inconvenient Study: The Cause of America’s Chronic Disease Epidemic Exposed,” the groundbreaking documentary produced by Del Bigtree that explores the alarming rise in chronic illness and neurodevelopmental disorders among children. In the film, Dr. Mumper brings both compassion and clarity to a complex issue — examining the links between early-life medical exposures and the explosion of childhood disease, while calling for true transparency, informed consent, and more effective, humane treatments. She has also authored a new book, "Kids and COVID: Costly Mistakes That Must Never Happen Again," which takes a deep dive into the catastrophic impacts on kids from Covid-era policies.
Dr. Elizabeth Mumper is the President & CEO of the Rimland Center for Integrative Medicine in Lynchburg, Virginia, where she leads two sister practices: Advocates for Children (general pediatrics) and Advocates for Families (autism and neurodevelopmental care). A former Medical Director of the Autism Research Institute and longtime University of Virginia faculty member, Dr. Mumper has spent decades bridging conventional pediatrics with integrative, evidence-based care.
She also serves on the faculty of the Medical Academy of Pediatric Special Needs (MAPS) and advises the Front Line COVID-19 Critical Care Alliance (FLCCC), where she authored the I-CARE: For Kids guide — a vital resource for families navigating post-COVID and vaccine-related pediatric challenges.
This week on VSRF Live, we’ll explore:
• Insights from An Inconvenient Study — what the data reveal about the chronic disease epidemic in children.
• The surge in autism, allergies, autoimmune conditions, and developmental disorders, and what clinicians are discovering about root causes.
• COVID-era fallout: how lockdowns, masking, and school disruption reshaped child health and learning.
• Reclaiming informed consent: what every parent should know before saying “yes” to medical interventions.
• Practical steps families can take to support healthier outcomes for their kids.
Join us Thursday for an illuminating, heartfelt discussion with one of the most trusted and courageous voices in pediatric medicine — a doctor unafraid to ask the hard questions and empower families with truth and hope.
📅 Thursday, November 13th
🕕 7 PM Eastern / 4 PM Pacific
